title: Global Intelligence Monitor
summary: A one-page briefing on world news, conflicts, politics and the economy in the week to 5 November 2026, with country profiles and a timeline since 1945.

news.headline: Putin puts Japan Tobacco's Russian assets under temporary state management
news.summary: A presidential decree transfers JTI stakes in four Russian factories (about 4,000 staff and roughly 40% of the cigarette market) to Industrial Assets / Promyshlennye Aktivy. JTI said it is assessing options; the move follows earlier seizures of Nestlé, Auchan, Metro and others.

news.headline: South Korea plans to expand anti-piracy mission closer to Hormuz
news.summary: Seoul will seek Assembly approval to extend the Cheonghae unit from the Gulf of Aden to waters south of Oman (~1,930 km radius), add a P-8A patrol aircraft and an EOD/mine team, and keep operations non-combat and outside the strait itself.

news.headline: Poland detains six over military-parts smuggling to Russia
news.summary: ABW and prosecutors say five Poles and a Russian woman ran a group that moved ammunition and weapons components to Kaliningrad (worth over 2 million zloty). Four face espionage charges and pretrial detention; the group operated at least June 2023–December 2025.

news.headline: Meloni urges EU to appoint a single Ukraine peace envoy
news.summary: In a letter to European Council President António Costa, Italy's PM said overlapping Miami, Oslo, Brussels and other formats make Europe look 'all over the place' and asked for the issue to go on the 13 Nov Dublin informal summit agenda, with a formal decision by December.

news.headline: Nasdaq down about 5.1% in afternoon US trade as AI stocks plunge
news.summary: Yahoo Finance showed the Nasdaq Composite near 24,413 (−5.1%) with the market still open; earlier reports had the S&P 500 off about 3.7–3.9% and the Dow about 2.9%, erasing Wednesday's post-election rally on data-centre and chip fears.

news.headline: Bank of England raises rates to 4%, first hike in over three years
news.summary: The MPC voted 8-1 to lift Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% (Catherine Mann wanted 4.25%), citing energy prices from the Iran war, and now expects UK inflation near 5% by mid-2027.

news.headline: Paraguay's President Peña resigns after Ueno Bank collapse
news.summary: Peña quit as the lower house moved to impeach him over the collapse of Ueno Bank, which says it has about 3 million customers. Vice President Pedro Alliana is due to be sworn in and serve until August 2028.

news.headline: Eisenkot gets 67 recommendations to form Israel's next government
news.summary: Joint List and Ra'am joined other opposition parties so Eisenkot has 67 Knesset recommendations vs 46 for Netanyahu; UTJ recommended no one. Herzog is expected to grant him the mandate after consultations wrap (28 days, plus up to 14).

news.headline: Iran says more tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz
news.summary: Iran's Guards and army said several tankers and a tugboat caught fire after hitting mines (not confirmed by maritime officials); UKMTO reported a tanker struck by two projectiles off Qatar. Oman says it is still discussing a joint Hormuz mechanism with Iran.

news.headline: Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials at the White House
news.summary: The first lady met representatives who arranged the six-day Oleshky ceasefire and called for a more 'enduring' peace, ahead of US-led trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 Nov.

news.headline: Komyshuvakha strike death toll rises to 42
news.summary: Police said up to 33 people may still be under rubble after Monday's Russian bombing of an aid point in Zaporizhzhia region; overnight both sides traded strikes as reconstruction talks resumed in Brussels.

news.headline: Hundreds of thousands protest over living costs across France
news.summary: The interior ministry counted more than 600,000 protesters, while the CGT claimed 1.57 million. PM Lecornu said he will convene a 'social conference' with unions and employers on Monday.

news.headline: Hoax bomb threats divert flights across Europe for a second time
news.summary: At least 27 flights were affected on Thursday (per Reuters), including Aer Lingus, Finnair, Wizz Air and LOT services; Finnair flights to Rome and Vienna landed safely and nothing was found.

news.headline: Joshua Wong jailed for 10 years under Hong Kong security law
news.summary: The pro-democracy activist, due for release in January, was sentenced for colluding with foreign forces under the 2020 national security law.

news.headline: ANC falls to about 32% in early South Africa local results
news.summary: With 36% of votes counted, the ANC had about 32% and the DA 27%; if it holds, the ANC would be down about 14 points on 2021. Full results are expected on Sunday.

news.headline: Sudan and Ethiopia expel each other's diplomats
news.summary: Ethiopia ordered six Sudanese diplomats out; Sudan accuses Ethiopia of backing the RSF, while Ethiopia accuses Sudan, Egypt and Eritrea of backing Tigray rebels. Both deny the claims.

news.headline: Developing-country debt hits a record $9.4tn
news.summary: The World Bank's International Debt Report says debt rose 5.5% last year, the fastest in four years, with the poorest countries paying the highest interest rates since the late 1980s.

news.headline: Democrats win control of both houses of the US Congress
news.summary: In the 3 November midterms, Democrats took the House and the Senate in a sharp rebuke of President Trump. Democracy Now reports at least 231 House seats and at least seven Senate pickups, with Mississippi and Alaska still too close to call.

news.headline: Trump says US military aid to Israel will end
news.summary: Trump told Fox News the roughly $4 billion in yearly US military aid to Israel will be cut off at the end of this year, though weapons sales will continue.

news.headline: Wall Street rallies after the Democratic sweep
news.summary: In early trade the Dow rose 2.3%, the S&P 500 1.72% and the Nasdaq 2.13%, as investors bet a divided Washington limits sharp policy shifts. Defence and data centre stocks fell.

news.headline: Tokyo stocks fall as Democrats retake Congress
news.summary: The Nikkei closed down 1.42% at 62,188.63 after briefly dropping toward 60,000. Tokyo said the US alliance stays essential whatever the result.

news.headline: US to host Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November
news.summary: US envoy Steve Witkoff said the working-level talks will cover post-war security, de-escalation, humanitarian steps and ending the war. They are the first three-way talks since February.

news.headline: Merz says Russia must finally negotiate seriously
news.summary: At a Berlin press conference with Zelenskyy, Chancellor Merz called the Abu Dhabi talks the right step but said he had seen no sign of serious Russian engagement.

news.headline: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz
news.summary: US officials called the strikes limited and defensive, after Iranian forces fired on US assets. It was the first US attack on the island since June, while Qatari mediation continues.

news.headline: Iran warns of response 'without geographical limitations'
news.summary: Armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi said Iran would meet any US or Israeli threat with an immediate response. Iran's seven-point plan to end the war is still with mediators.

news.headline: Israel certifies election results; Herzog starts coalition talks
news.summary: Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats, Eisenkot's opposition bloc 48 and Arab-led parties a record 19, so no bloc has the 61 needed. The election committee rejected fraud claims.

news.headline: Saudi crown prince hosts Syria's President al-Sharaa
news.summary: Mohammed bin Salman received Ahmed al-Sharaa in Riyadh for talks on security, counterterrorism and economic ties.

news.headline: Iotova re-elected president of Bulgaria
news.summary: Incumbent Iliana Iotova won Sunday's runoff with 57.58% of the vote against former caretaker PM Andrey Gurov.

news.headline: Spain's transport minister quits after deadly train crashes
news.summary: Oscar Puente resigned after the 28 October Urda crash. Deputy PM Carlos Cuerpo runs the ministry until the 29 November snap election.

news.headline: Eurozone inflation rises to 4.0%
news.summary: Eurostat's flash estimate for October is 4.0%, up from 3.8%, driven by energy prices up 20.8% on a year earlier.

news.headline: Montenegro could sign EU accession treaty in June 2027
news.summary: The European Commission said talks with Montenegro could close by the end of this year, the first since Croatia in 2011.

news.headline: Cyberattack hits French blood banks
news.summary: Officials said no samples were compromised. It follows reports of supermarket fridges in several European countries being remotely taken over.

news.headline: British health worker with Ebola to be flown from DR Congo to UK
news.summary: The patient is stable. DR Congo's outbreak passed 5,000 deaths by 30 October, its deadliest on record, with cases also in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.

news.headline: South Africans vote in local elections seen as a test for the ANC
news.summary: Voters chose councillors in 257 municipalities amid anger over poor services. Final results were not yet out.

news.headline: Drone attacks push Sudan's power grid toward collapse
news.summary: At least 15 substations have been hit since early October. The UN envoy says talks with the RSF and its allies are expected before Christmas.

news.headline: Prabowo sacks chief of staff over alleged wiretapping
news.summary: Indonesia's president dismissed Listyo Sigit Prabowo after he and two senior police officers were detained over alleged illegal wiretapping of the president and others.

news.headline: Anwar shores up government with opposition deal
news.summary: Malaysia's prime minister signed a confidence and supply agreement with 13 opposition MPs backing the 2027 budget and reforms.

news.headline: Anwar warns Malaysia is a cyberattack target
news.summary: The prime minister ordered top-level security briefings and urged the public to stay calm and alert.

news.headline: Xi pledges 'high-standard opening up' before Shanghai import expo
news.summary: Xi said China will keep economic globalisation open and inclusive, as Beijing urged APEC members to uphold free trade.

news.headline: Burnham says US midterms create an 'opportunity'
news.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the result lets the world focus on the cost of living and ending the Iran war.

news.headline: Brazil publishes first global roadmap to phase out fossil fuels
news.summary: Brazil urged countries to start planning now for a voluntary phase-out of coal, oil and gas, days before COP31.

conflicts.name: Russia-Ukraine war
conflicts.latest: Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian officials on 5 Nov after the Oleshky ceasefire; Meloni pressed the EU for a single peace envoy. US-led trilateral talks remain set for Abu Dhabi on 10-11 Nov while strikes continue.

conflicts.name: US/Israel-Iran war
conflicts.latest: Iran says tankers/tug caught fire on unauthorised Hormuz routes (unconfirmed by maritime officials); South Korea plans to expand anti-piracy patrols toward waters south of Oman. Oil recovered toward ~$97 Brent.

conflicts.name: Houthis vs Saudi-led coalition (Yemen)
conflicts.latest: Coalition says it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile fired toward the Medina region on 5 Nov; attacks on Saudi sites continue. The 2022 UN truce has broken down.

conflicts.name: Gaza
conflicts.parties: Israel, Hamas (Egypt, Qatar, Turkey, US mediating)
conflicts.latest: The October 2025 ceasefire holds loosely; a Hamas delegation in Cairo urges mediators to press Israel to implement the deal and move to the next phase.

conflicts.name: Israel-Hezbollah (Lebanon)
conflicts.latest: Israeli shelling and a drone strike in southern Lebanon; Israel presses Beirut to keep Hezbollah out of any renewed Iran war.

conflicts.name: Sudan civil war
conflicts.parties: Sudanese Armed Forces, Rapid Support Forces
conflicts.latest: Drone strikes on power and fuel sites deepen outages and hunger; Sudan and Ethiopia expelled each other's diplomats on 5 Nov over claims of backing rivals. No ceasefire.

history.title: State of Israel founded; Berlin Blockade
history.detail: Israel declares independence and the first Arab-Israeli war follows; the Soviets blockade West Berlin.

history.title: NATO formed; People's Republic of China founded
history.detail: Mao Zedong proclaims the PRC; the USSR tests its first atomic bomb.

history.title: Korean War
history.detail: Ends in an armistice that still divides the peninsula.

history.title: Warsaw Pact and Bandung Conference
history.detail: Soviet bloc alliance formed; Asian and African states meet in Bandung, Indonesia.

history.title: Sputnik; Malaya independent; Treaty of Rome
history.detail: Space race starts; the European Economic Community is founded.

history.title: Year of Africa

history.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
history.detail: The closest the superpowers came to nuclear war.

history.title: Six-Day War; ASEAN founded
history.detail: Israel takes the West Bank, Gaza, Sinai and Golan Heights; five states found ASEAN.

history.title: Yom Kippur War and oil crisis
history.detail: Arab oil embargo quadruples oil prices.

history.title: Fall of Saigon
history.detail: The Vietnam War ends with the country unified under the North.

history.title: Iranian Revolution; Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
history.detail: The Islamic Republic is founded; China begins market reforms under Deng Xiaoping.

history.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
history.detail: Revolutions sweep Eastern Europe; Tiananmen Square crackdown in China.

history.detail: Iraq invades Kuwait in August; the Gulf War follows in 1991.

history.title: Soviet Union dissolves
history.detail: Fifteen independent states, including Russia and Ukraine, emerge; the Cold War ends.

history.title: End of apartheid; Rwandan genocide
history.detail: Nelson Mandela becomes South Africa's president.

history.title: Asian financial crisis; Hong Kong handover
history.detail: Currency crashes hit Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia and South Korea.

history.title: 9/11 attacks
history.detail: The US launches the war in Afghanistan; China joins the WTO.

history.detail: Saddam Hussein is overthrown.
